newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks end just up as NAB props up market.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks end just up as NAB props up market.

text.p: Australian shares ended just one point up on Thursday with weaker resources counteracted by a buoyant banking sector which was inspired by sector leader National Australia Bank after it reported strong first quarter earnings.
The key share barometer, the All Ordinaries index, closed one point firmer at 2,434.5.

National Australia released its profit figures 15 minutes before the open and its shares climbed steadily from the start of trade, investors reacting favourably to its 18 percent rise in first quarter pre-tax earnings to A$921 million (US$709 million).
National Australia Bank shares closed 50 cents higher at A$15.51.
"NAB came through with a very good result and consequently banks led the way for the rest of the day," said a dealer from Brisbane firm, Morgan Stockbroking.

The dealer said that action amongst the major issues was subdued but there was plenty of speculative interest amongst small gold explorers with interests in the prospective Gawler Craton region of South Australia.
"The smaller miners are still releasing quarterlies so this is where a lot of investor attention is being focused," he said.
Holding back the market was continued selling of major resource issues BHP and CRA. BHP shares ended nine cents weaker at A$18.16 while CRA stock fell 25 cents to A$19.25.
Despite interest at the speculative end of the market the gold sector finished weaker after the price of bullion fell to the US$350 level in New York on Wednesday.
Dealers said the direction on Friday would remain strongly linked to the Dow's moves but in the absence of any strong leads the market was likely to continue to drift sideways.
